inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-07-31, 10-Q), matched to the same balance-sheet date as net debt. Basic shares on the 2026-09-03 cover page were 190.16M after continued buybacks; those post-quarter repurchases are left out of both the count and net debt, which is slightly conservative. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (SEC XBRL): cash-flow SBC add-back $70.5M + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $24.8M (financing). Cooper publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $290.1M; 9M FY2026 $447.2M (Q3 alone $339.2M) and authorization raised by $1B to ~$1.5B after the CooperSurgical strategic review ended. Cooper is an active repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~1.0 (diversified med-device, low cyclicality), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.3%. Debt ~18% of EV at market (net debt $2.39B vs ~$10.7B market cap), pre-tax cost ~5.5% (FY2025 interest expense $100M on ~$2.5B), after tax ~4.5%. WACC ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5% and held identical across scenarios so risk is charged once, in the scenario paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost sits inside operating income and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; operating lease liabilities ($278M at FY2025) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (US operating company: contact lenses + women's health/fertility; no bank/REIT/holdco features; first valuation of COO, no prior model to match). FY0 = FY2025 actual (Oct year-end); year 1 = FY2026, pinned to guidance mid-point ($4.229-4.252B -> +3.6%). EBITDA margin is GAAP EBITDA plus SBC (pre-SBC), i.e. it keeps Cooper's habitually recurring restructuring/integration charges inside the margin rather than using the non-GAAP figure. FY2026 run-rate: Q1 32.0%, Q3 31.2%, Q2 ~32.5% ex the $272M litigation charge; FY2025 27.6%, FY2024 29.7%. The Q2 FY2026 litigation charge is not in the flows; its unpaid net accrual is deducted in the equity bridge instead. Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS includes a $307.2M discrete UK tax benefit that is ignored (cash tax path uses FY2025 cash taxes paid $100M, ~15% of operating income, stepping to the guided ~17.5% FY2027 rate). D&A = depreciation ($178M) + acquired-intangible amortization ($199M), 9.2% of revenue, tapering as intangibles run off; it only affects the tax shield. Working capital: receivables + inventory - payables ~ $1.45B (34% of revenue), so growth consumes cash (negative capture). Interest income is not stripped: Cooper is net debt. Net debt uses total debt excluding operating leases.

equity_bridge.item: Litigation accrual net of insurance receivable (fertility settlement / Paragard)
equity_bridge.note: LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue $325.8M less LossContingencyReceivable $53.8M at 2026-07-31 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q XBRL). Charged in Q2 FY2026 ($271.6M loss in period), not yet paid, not in total debt. Paragard exposure beyond this accrual is not quantified and is carried in the bear case and the bear weight.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR (7.3%, flattered by FY2022-23 acquisitions) cut toward FY2026's guided +3.6% and management's mid-single-digit organic commentary
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (16.6%) diverges >30% from revenue (11.0%) and EPS (9.2%): FY2021 book value jumped ~$2.1B on a one-off deferred-tax-asset recognition (FY2021 NI $2.94B). Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020 base is COVID-depressed, so all 5yr CAGRs overstate. EPS 5yr CAGR uses FY2020 EPS restated for the Feb-2024 4:1 split ($4.85/4). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 117.3, FY2022 379.4, FY2023 139.8, FY2024 182.7, FY2025 338.4. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-3.7%) is below reported (-1.3%): SBC plus withholding grew from $71M to $95M while FCF went sideways through the FY2023-24 capacity-capex cycle. TTM to Q3 FY2026 reported FCF ~ $678M (record Q3 $273M) as capex fell to ~8% of revenue.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the guided mid-point; CooperVision returns to mid-single-digit reported growth once the US channel destock laps, MiSight keeps compounding double-digit ex-China, CooperSurgical grows low-to-mid single digit as fertility offsets Paragard erosion. Margin expands ~1.5pp as capex and restructuring normalise.

bull.narrative: Myopia management becomes standard of care in Europe, Japan and the Americas and China recovers; the 5,000-door US salesforce expansion and pulled-forward launches win share from J&J Vision and Alcon; fertility genomics/lab platform compounds high-single-digit. Operating leverage plus lower capex lift margins to peer levels.

bear.narrative: The flat CooperVision prints are share loss, not destocking: J&J and Alcon outspend on daily silicone hydrogel and myopia entrants erode MiSight pricing while China stays soft. Paragard loses its non-hormonal monopoly and the MDL (4,000+ cases, exposure above insurance) keeps cash settlements flowing as recurring charges. Global minimum tax pushes cash tax to 20%.

scenario_narratives.base: CooperVision consumption growth (mid-single-digit per management) reappears in reported revenue after the FY2026 US channel inventory reduction laps; MiSight grows ~15-20% ex-China; CooperSurgical fertility offsets IUD competition. Revenue compounds ~4-5% for five years, fading to 3%; pre-SBC EBITDA margin drifts from 31% to 32.5% as capex steps down from the FY2023-25 capacity build (10.9% -> ~6%). Cash tax follows guidance to ~17.5-18%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Myopia management is the axis: MiSight/MyDay MiSight approvals in Japan, UK and Europe and a China recovery turn it into a multi-hundred-million-dollar double-digit grower; the expanded US sales footprint and pulled-forward pipeline regain share in torics/multifocals; fertility genomics compounds. Growth 6.5-7% for four years, margins to 34.5%, capex to 5.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Contact-lens share loss to J&J Vision and Alcon is structural, not timing; China myopia stays soft and competitors narrow MiSight's clinical lead; Paragard's monopoly ends and the MDL (4,000+ cases, exposure potentially above insurance) produces further settlements beyond the $272M net accrual already deducted. Growth ~2.5%, margin compresses to 29.5%, cash tax 20%, 14x terminal cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because Paragard mass-tort exposure beyond the accrual is unquantified and management says it may exceed insurance, and because several quarters of flat CooperVision revenue leave share loss a live explanation. Base 50% as FY2026 guidance is intact and FCF is at a record. Bull cut to 25% because it needs MiSight adoption, a China recovery and share regain to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF with SBC and equity-award withholding taxes expensed and the share count held flat (Cooper is an active repurchaser). Margins built from GAAP-inclusive components so Cooper's recurring 'one-time' charges stay in the flows; the one quantified litigation liability is deducted in the bridge. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) reported as a memo band.
key_risks_to_valuation: Paragard MDL: 4,000+ cases, loss probable, exposure potentially above insurance; only the $272M net accrual is deducted
CooperVision revenue flat for several quarters; destock vs share loss unresolved
Terminal value dominates: a 10-year fade at 8.5% WACC with an 18x cap
FY2027 tax step-up to ~17.5% and potential Pillar Two creep
Recurring restructuring/litigation charges historically 2-4pp of revenue; margin path assumes they shrink
